questions.q: What does a capability evaluation primarily try to measure?
options: How many parameters the model has
The ceiling of what the model could be made to do under aggressive, adversarial elicitation, regardless of default behavior
How fast the model responds to a typical user prompt
How much it costs to run the model in production
questions.explain: Capability evaluations use fine-tuning, scaffolding, and best-known prompting techniques to find the most the model could be made to do, not what it does by default.

questions.q: What does a safety (alignment) evaluation primarily try to measure?
options: The model's actual behavior under realistic, naturalistic usage conditions
The theoretical maximum capability the model could ever reach
The model's training data size
The number of parameters tuned during fine-tuning
questions.explain: Safety evaluations characterize the typical behavior distribution — what the model actually does when ordinary users and adversaries interact with it normally.

questions.q: Why can a model pass a safety evaluation and still harbor a dangerous capability?
options: Because safety evaluations are always run on a different model than the one deployed
Because fine-tuning or scaffolding can surface a capability that naturalistic use would never trigger, and a safety eval never applies that kind of pressure
Because safety evaluations are graded by the model itself with no oversight
Because dangerous capabilities only appear after a model is deleted and retrained
questions.explain: A safety eval measures default behavior, not what adversarial elicitation could surface — so a latent capability can sit undetected until a capability eval specifically goes looking for it.

questions.q: What role do capability thresholds play in frameworks like Anthropic's Responsible Scaling Policy or OpenAI's Preparedness Framework?
options: They have no practical effect on deployment decisions
Crossing a defined threshold on a capability evaluation triggers mandatory new safeguards, regardless of how safely the model behaves by default
They only apply after a model has already been deployed to the public
They replace the need for any safety evaluation entirely
questions.explain: These policies tie specific, pre-defined capability levels to mandatory safeguards that activate on crossing the threshold, independent of the model's naturalistic behavior.

questions.q: Why does this lesson argue that neither capability evals nor safety evals are sufficient on their own?
options: Because they measure different things — a worst-case ceiling versus a typical-case behavior distribution — and a deployment decision needs both
Because both types of evaluation always produce identical results anyway
Because only capability evaluations are ever useful in practice
Because safety evaluations have been fully deprecated by the field
questions.explain: Capability evals bound what's possible in the worst case; safety evals describe what actually happens under normal use. A complete picture requires both.
